title: ArgoCD Enterprise GitOps, ApplicationSets & Sync Waves
summary: Master enterprise GitOps with ArgoCD: Application CRDs, multi-tenant ApplicationSets, declarative sync waves, hooks, health checks, self-healing automated sync, and rollouts integration.
learningObjectives: Author and reconcile declarative ArgoCD Application custom resources with automated sync policies.
Orchestrate multi-step deployments with ArgoCD sync waves (argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave) and PreSync hooks.
Manage enterprise multi-cluster deployments using ArgoCD ApplicationSets and matrix generators.

curriculumModules.title: ArgoCD Application Architecture & Declarative CRDs
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: ArgoCD runs as a Kubernetes controller that continuously reconciles git repositories against cluster state. Applications are defined declaratively via Application CRDs specifying repoURL, path, targetRevision, and destination cluster/namespace.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy ArgoCD in a dedicated argocd namespace with automated self-healing, prune enabled, and strict RBAC projects restricting tenant destination namespaces.

curriculumModules.title: Sync Waves, Resource Hooks & Multi-Cluster ApplicationSets
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Sync waves order resource application into phases using the argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave annotation (e.g. wave 0 for ConfigMaps/Secrets, wave 1 for Databases, wave 2 for Applications). PreSync and PostSync hooks execute database migrations and verification tests.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Apply wave 0 to shared dependencies, wave 1 to backend workloads, and wave 2 to frontend ingress routes, verifying health before progressing to subsequent waves.

labs.title: Deploying and Synchronizing an ArgoCD Application
labs.scenario: Deploy an ArgoCD Application resource named frontend-portal in namespace argocd that targets repo https://github.com/kubelabs/frontend.git at path deploy/prod with destination namespace production. Run argocd app sync frontend-portal to achieve Synced and Healthy status, resulting in a running Deployment frontend-portal in namespace production.
labs.productionContext: Declarative Application CRDs allow entire Kubernetes application stacks to be version-controlled, reviewed, and deployed automatically across dev, staging, and production clusters.
objectives: Create and apply Application manifest for frontend-portal in namespace argocd.
Execute argocd app sync frontend-portal to reconcile live cluster resources.
Verify Application is Synced and Healthy and Deployment frontend-portal is running in namespace production.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: frontend-portal
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/kubelabs/frontend.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: deploy/prod
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true

steps.title: Apply ArgoCD Application manifest
steps.instruction: Save the Application specification to /gitops/frontend-app.yaml and apply it to namespace argocd.

steps.title: Synchronize application via ArgoCD CLI
steps.instruction: Trigger a sync on frontend-portal using the argocd CLI to reconcile resources into the production namespace.

validationRules.description: Application frontend-portal is Synced and Healthy
validationRules.name: frontend-portal

validationRules.description: Deployment frontend-portal exists in namespace production
validationRules.name: frontend-portal
validationRules.remediation: Ensure frontend-portal deployment is reconciled in namespace production

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /gitops/frontend-app.yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: frontend-portal
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/kubelabs/frontend.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: deploy/prod
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Application frontend-portal status is OutOfSync or not found.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The Application manifest was not applied or argocd app sync was not run.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Apply /gitops/frontend-app.yaml and run argocd app sync frontend-portal.

labs.title: Phased Rollout Orchestration with ArgoCD Sync Waves
labs.scenario: To prevent application startup failures, database ConfigMap dependencies must be ready before backend pods start. Apply ConfigMap backend-config with annotation argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '0' and Deployment backend-api with annotation argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '1' in namespace production.
labs.productionContext: Sync waves allow Kubernetes resources to be applied in a deterministic sequence, guaranteeing database migrations and secrets exist before dependent microservices start.
objectives: Deploy ConfigMap backend-config with sync-wave 0 in namespace production.
Deploy Deployment backend-api with sync-wave 1 in namespace production.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: backend-config
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0"
data:
  API_TIMEOUT: "30s"
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: backend-api
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: backend-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/backend-api:v2.1.0

steps.title: Define and apply sync wave manifests
steps.instruction: Save the ConfigMap and Deployment manifests with argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave annotations to /gitops/sync-waves.yaml and apply to production.

steps.title: Verify sync wave annotations
steps.instruction: Inspect annotations on both resources to confirm wave ordering (0 for config, 1 for workload).
steps.commandHint:
kubectl get cm backend-config -n production -o yaml
kubectl get deploy backend-api -n production -o yaml

validationRules.name: backend-config
validationRules.remediation: Add annotation argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '0' to ConfigMap backend-config

validationRules.name: backend-api
validationRules.remediation: Add annotation argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '1' to Deployment backend-api

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /gitops/sync-waves.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: backend-config
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0"
data:
  API_TIMEOUT: "30s"
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: backend-api
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: backend-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/backend-api:v2.1.0
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.cause: The annotation key or value was incorrectly formatted.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Ensure metadata.annotations contains 'argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave': '0' on the ConfigMap and '1' on the Deployment.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the purpose of ArgoCD sync waves (argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave)?
options: To compress container images across network links before synchronization.
To establish phased resource application ordering so foundational dependencies (CRDs, Namespaces, ConfigMaps) are healthy before application pods start.
To distribute pod scheduling evenly across AWS Availability Zones.
To automatically generate TLS certificates via Let's Encrypt.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Sync waves allow engineers to order resource application phases (negative waves first, then 0, 1, 2, etc.). ArgoCD waits for resources in a given wave to become Healthy before starting the next wave.

assessmentQuestions.question: In an ArgoCD Application custom resource, what does syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal do?
options: It automatically restarts worker nodes when memory exceeds 90%.
It automatically reverts manual mutations made directly to the live cluster back to the state declared in Git.
It generates automated pull requests when a container vulnerability is detected.
It rolls back the cluster to the previous Kubernetes minor version.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: With selfHeal enabled, ArgoCD continuously reconciles the cluster and automatically overrides uncommitted out-of-band changes with the desired Git state, preventing configuration drift.
